extracted.intended_audience: parties, counsel, presiding officers, and NRC staff participating in or administering NRC adjudicatory and legislative hearings (10 CFR Part 2)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedural requirements and timelines governing expedited proceedings with oral hearings, legislative hearings, and model hearing milestones under 10 CFR Part 2. Covers who may participate, filing and hearing procedures, evidentiary limits, decision and appeal processes, and presiding officer and staff roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for granting a stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the requestor will be irreparably injured unless a stay is granted; Whether the requestor has made a strong showing that it is likely to prevail on the merits; Whether the granting of a stay would harm other participants; and Where the public interest lies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission action — written opinion and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of a hearing, the Commission will issue a written opinion including its decision on the license transfer application and the reasons for the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on issues designated for hearing under § 2.309 will be based on the record developed at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart N purpose, scope, and cessation deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: to provide simplified procedures for the expeditious resolution of disputes among parties in an informal hearing process; provisions govern adjudicatory proceedings conducted under this subpart in accordance with § 2.310.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subpart shall cease to have effect on January 8, 2027, unless the NRC determines the cessation deadline should be extended (to no more than 5 years) after offering public input on costs and benefits and considering that input; the NRC will publish its determination in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on written pleadings and briefs (Subpart N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where provided otherwise in this subpart or specifically requested by the presiding officer or the Commission, written pleadings and briefs (regardless of whether they are in the form of a letter, a formal legal submission, or otherwise) are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference scheduling requests may be written
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to schedule a conference to consider oral motions may be in writing and served on the Presiding officer and the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for summary disposition and motions for reconsideration not permitted (Subpart N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions for summary disposition before the hearing has concluded and motions for reconsideration to the presiding officer or the Commission are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: All motions must be presented and argued orally
rubrics_metrics.description: All motions must be presented and argued orally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulings reflected in written decision; transcript acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer will reflect all rulings on motions and other requests from the parties in a written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A verbatim transcript of oral rulings satisfies this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery requests generally disallowed (Subpart N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for the information disclosure requirements set forth in subpart C of this part, requests for discovery will not be entertained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer may issue orders for orderly conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may issue written orders and rulings necessary for the orderly and effective conduct of the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer to other subpart if Subpart N not appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If it becomes apparent at any time before a hearing is held that a proceeding selected for adjudication under this subpart is not appropriate for application of this subpart, the presiding officer or the Commission may, on its own motion or at the request of a party, order the proceeding to continue under another appropriate subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discontinued because not appropriate, the presiding officer may issue written orders necessary for orderly continuation under another subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for cross-examination (oral motion standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may present an oral motion to the presiding officer to permit cross-examination by the parties on particular admitted contentions or issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer may allow cross-examination by the parties if he or she determines that cross-examination by the parties is necessary for the development of an adequate record for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: NRC staff action during pendency of hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pendency of any hearing under this subpart, consistent with the NRC staff's findings and as authorized by law, the NRC staff is expected to promptly issue its approval or denial of the application, or take other appropriate action on the matter that is the subject of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the NRC staff takes action it must notify the presiding officer and the parties and explain why public health and safety is protected and why the action is in accord with the common defense and security. Staff action is effective upon issuance except in matters involving: (1) application to construct and/or operate a production or utilization facility; (2) application for construction and operation of an ISFSI located at a site other than a reactor site or a monitored retrievable storage facility under 10 CFR part 72; or (3) licensing actions that involve significant hazards considerations as defined in 10 CFR 50.92 or 53.1520.

rubrics_metrics.name: When NRC staff must be a party
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC staff is not required to be a party to proceedings under this subpart, except where: (i) the proceeding involves an application denied by the NRC staff or an enforcement action proposed by the staff; or (ii) the presiding officer determines that resolution of any issue would be materially aided by staff participation and orders staff to participate for the identified issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordered to participate, the presiding officer shall identify the issue(s) and set forth the basis for that determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff notification and disclosure obligations if participating
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fifteen (15) days of the issuance of the order granting requests for hearing/petitions to intervene and admitting contentions, the NRC staff shall notify the presiding officer and the parties whether it desires to participate as a party, and identify the contentions on which it wishes to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If staff desires to be a party thereafter, it shall notify and make the disclosures required by § 2.336(b)(3) through (5) unless accompanied by an affidavit explaining why disclosures cannot be provided with the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff party status confers full party rights/responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the NRC staff chooses to participate as a party, it shall have all the rights and responsibilities of a party with respect to the admitted contention/matter in controversy on which the staff chooses to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing conference timing and modality
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than forty (40) days after the order granting requests for hearing/petitions to intervene, the presiding officer shall conduct a prehearing conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the discretion of the presiding officer, the prehearing conference may be held in person or by telephone or through the use of video conference technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing witness identification and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: At the prehearing conference, each party shall provide the presiding officer and the parties participating in the conference with a statement identifying each witness the party plans to present at the hearing and a written summary of the oral and written testimony of each proposed witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prehearing conference is not held in person, each party shall forward the summaries to the presiding officer and the other parties by such means that will ensure receipt by the commencement of the prehearing conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing topics to be addressed and presiding officer order
rubrics_metrics.description: At the prehearing conference, the parties shall describe the results of their efforts to settle or narrow contentions, provide an agreed statement of facts, identify witnesses to present, provide questions or question areas for the presiding officer to cover with witnesses, and discuss other pertinent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the conclusion of the conference, the presiding officer will issue an order specifying the issues to be addressed at the hearing, setting forth any agreements reached, include the scheduled date for any remaining hearing, and address other matters as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for holding a hearing after prehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than twenty (20) days after the conclusion of the prehearing conference, the presiding officer shall hold a hearing on any contention that remains in dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the beginning of the hearing, the presiding officer shall enter into the record all agreements reached by the parties before the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and transcript as official record
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing will be recorded stenographically or by other means under the presiding officer's supervision; a transcript will be prepared from the recording that will be the sole official transcript of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript will be prepared by an official reporter; except as limited, the transcript will be available for inspection in the agency's public records system. Copies are available to parties and the public from the reporter on payment. If videotaped, copies may be made available on payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to hearings with limited closures
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings will be open to the public, unless portions of the hearings involving proprietary or other protectable information are closed in accordance with the Commission's regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary limits on oral testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer will not receive oral evidence that is irrelevant, immaterial, unreliable or unduly repetitious. Testimony will be under oath or affirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer may question witnesses; parties may not
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer may question witnesses who testify at the hearing, but the parties may not do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument and final statements only (no written post-hearing briefs unless ordered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party may present oral argument and a final statement of position at the close of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written post-hearing briefs and proposed findings are not permitted unless ordered by the presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial decision timing and bench decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where practicable, the presiding officer will render a decision from the bench and state issues, findings of fact and conclusions of law on each issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rendered from the bench, the decision and order must be reduced to writing and transmitted to the parties as soon as practicable, but not later than 20 days after the hearing ends. If not rendered from the bench, a written decision will be issued not later than 30 days after the hearing ends. Approval of the Chief Administrative Judge is required for extensions; in no event may a written decision be issued later than 60 days after the hearing ends without the express approval of the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and filing of presiding officer's written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer's written decision must be served on the parties and filed with the Commission when issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of presiding officer's initial decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer's initial decision is effective and constitutes the final action of the Commission twenty-five (25) days after the date of issuance of the written decision unless any party appeals to the Commission in accordance with § 2.1407 or the Commission takes review sua sponte or the regulations specify other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal filing deadline and prerequisite to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 25 days after service of a written initial decision, a party may file a written appeal seeking the Commission's review on the grounds specified in paragraph (b) of § 2.1407. Unless otherwise authorized by law, a party must file an appeal with the Commission before seeking judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal content and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal under this section may not be longer than twenty (20) pages and must contain: (i) a concise statement of the specific rulings and decisions that are being appealed; (ii) a concise statement (including record citations) where the matters of fact or law raised in the appeal were previously raised before the presiding officer and, if they were not, why they could not have been raised; (iii) a concise statement why, in the appellant's view, the decision or action is erroneous; and (iv) a concise statement why the Commission should review the decision or action, with particular reference to the grounds specified in paragraph (b) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer to appeal by other parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any other party to the proceeding may, within 25 days after service of the appeal, file an answer supporting or opposing the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The answer may not be longer than 20 pages and should concisely address the matters specified in paragraph (a)(2) of § 2.1407. The appellant does not have a right to reply. Unless it directs additional filings or oral arguments, the Commission will decide the appeal on the basis of the permitted filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission standards for granting review on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering the appeal, the Commission will give due weight to the existence of a substantial question with respect to: (1) a finding of material fact that is clearly erroneous or in conflict with a finding as to the same fact in a different proceeding; (2) a necessary legal conclusion that is without governing precedent or is a departure from, or contrary to, established law; (3) a substantial and important question of law, policy or discretion raised by the appeal; (4) that the conduct of the proceeding involved a prejudicial procedural error; or (5) any other consideration which the Commission may deem to be in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of final agency decision for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a decision becomes final agency action, the Secretary shall transmit the decision to the NRC staff for action in accordance with the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of Subpart O (Legislative Hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for simplified, legislative hearing procedures to be used, at the Commission's sole discretion, in design certification rulemaking hearings under subpart B of part 52 or subpart H of part 53, and in developing a record to assist the Commission in resolving a petition filed under § 2.335(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subpart also contains a cessation deadline provision similar to other subparts and may be time-limited unless extended following public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — demonstrative and documentary information
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative information means physical things, not constituting documentary information. Documentary information means information, ordinarily contained in documents or electronic files, but may also include photographs and digital audio files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission discretion to hold legislative hearing and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may, in its discretion, hold a legislative hearing in either a design certification rulemaking under § 52.51(b) or § 53.1242(b)(2), or a proceeding where a question has been certified to it under § 2.335(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission decides to hold a legislative hearing it must provide notice with specified information (see § 2.1502(c)); notices must be published in the Federal Register and on the NRC website as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission must identify issues for legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission decides to hold a legislative hearing, it shall identify with specificity the issues on which it wishes to compile a record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required information to be included in the notice/order per § 2.1502(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of parties and interested governmental bodies for legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: For hearings associated with a question certified to the Commission under § 2.335(d), the Commission shall identify the parties and interested State(s), governmental bodies, and Federally-recognized Indian Tribe under § 2.315(c) who may participate in the legislative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1502(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of persons/entities to be invited
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall identify persons and entities that may, in the discretion of the Commission, be invited to participate in the legislative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1502(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for permitting request-to-participate by others
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall indicate whether other persons and entities may request, in accordance with § 2.1504, to participate in the legislative hearing, and the criteria that the Commission or presiding officer will use in determining whether to permit such participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1502(c)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify who will conduct the legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice/order must indicate whether the Commission or a presiding officer will conduct the legislative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1502(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify any special procedures for legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must specify any special procedures to be used in the legislative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1502(c)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set dates for submissions and commencement of oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice/order must set the dates for submission of requests to participate in the legislative hearing, submission of written statements and demonstrative and documentary information, and commencement of the oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1502(c)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify location of oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice/order must specify the location where the oral hearing is to be held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinarily, oral hearings will be held in the Washington, DC metropolitan area. (Required per § 2.1502(c)(8).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer authority in legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission appoints a presiding officer to conduct the legislative hearing, the presiding officer shall be responsible for expeditious development of a sufficient record on the Commission-identified issues, consistent with the Commission's direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer has the authority otherwise accorded under §§ 2.319(a),(c),(e),(g),(h),(i), 2.324, and 2.333 to control the course of the proceeding, and may exercise any other authority granted by the Commission in accordance with § 2.1502(c)(6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of request to participate in legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or entity who wishes to participate in a legislative hearing shall submit a request to participate by the date specified in the notice. The request must address: (1) a summary of the person's position on the subject matter of the legislative hearing; and (2) the specific information, expertise or experience that the person possesses with respect to the subject matter of the legislative hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1504(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on requests to participate — timing and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or presiding officer shall, within ten (10) days of the date specified for submission of requests to participate, determine whether the person or entity has met the criteria and issue an order informing them of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A presiding officer's determinations in this regard are final and not subject to any motion for reconsideration or appeal to the Commission; and the Commission's determinations are final and not subject to a motion for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of NRC staff in legislative hearings (non-advocate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC staff shall be available to answer Commission or presiding officer questions on staff-prepared documents, provide additional information or documentation that may be available to the staff, and provide other assistance requested without requiring the NRC staff to assume the role of an advocate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC staff may request to participate in the legislative hearing by providing notice to the Commission or presiding officer within the time period established for submitting a request to participate; or, if no notice is provided under § 2.1502(b)(2), within ten (10) days of the Commission's order announcing its determination to conduct a legislative hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statements and documentary/demonstrative submissions deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants shall file written statements on the Commission-identified issues, and may submit documentary and demonstrative information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written statements, copies of documentary information, and a list and short description of any demonstrative information to be submitted must be received by the NRC (and in certain hearings, by the parties in the related proceeding) no later than ten (10) days before the commencement of the oral hearing. (See § 2.1506.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness grouping and order of appearance notice timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Not less than five (5) days before the commencement of the oral hearing, the presiding officer shall issue an order setting forth the grouping and order of appearance of the witnesses at the oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order shall be filed upon all participants by email or facsimile transmission if possible, otherwise by overnight mail. (See § 2.1507(a).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission/presiding officer questioning and recommended questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or presiding officer may question witnesses. Neither will ordinarily permit participants to submit recommended questions for them to propound to witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the Commission or presiding officer believe that the conduct of the oral hearing will be expedited and that consideration of such proposed questions will assist in developing a more focused hearing record, they may, in their discretion, permit participants to submit recommended questions. (See § 2.1507(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hearing additional submissions (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission or presiding officer may request, or upon request of a participant may, in the presiding officer's discretion, permit the submission of additional information following the close of the oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information must be submitted no later than five (5) days after the close of the oral hearing and must be served at the same time upon all participants at the oral hearing. (See § 2.1507(c).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer certification to Commission after legislative hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission is not acting as a presiding officer, the presiding officer shall, within thirty (30) days following the close of the legislative hearing record, certify the record to the Commission on each of the issues identified by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in presiding officer's certification to Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer's certification for each Commission-identified issue shall contain: a transcript of the oral phase of the legislative hearing; a list of all participants; a list of all witnesses and their affiliation; a list, and copies of, all documentary information submitted with ADAMS accession numbers; all demonstrative information submitted; any written answers submitted by the NRC staff with ADAMS accession numbers; a certification that all documentary information has been entered into ADAMS and placed on the NRC website unless protected from disclosure; a certification that the record contains sufficient information for the Commission to make a reasoned determination; and, at the presiding officer's option, a summary of the record and a proposed resolution with supporting basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required per § 2.1508(b)(1)-(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte communications and separation of functions in legislative hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2.347 applies in a legislative hearing. Section 2.348 applies in a legislative hearing only where the hearing addresses an issue certified to the Commission under § 2.335(d), and then only with respect to the underlying contested matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Milestones for hearings under Subpart G
rubrics_metrics.description: Model schedule milestones for enforcement action hearings under 10 CFR Part 2, Subpart G (to be used by presiding officer as a guideline in developing a hearing schedule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key milestones (examples): within 20 days of enforcement order: answer filed; within 100 days: presiding officer issues order on hearing request; within 25 days of presiding officer decision granting hearing: set initial schedule; within 145 days: discovery complete; within 155 days: motions for summary disposition due; within 235 days: decisions on summary disposition; within 245 days: prehearing conference/setting schedule; within 275 days: written testimony filed; within 90 days of end of evidentiary hearing: presiding officer issues initial decision. The presiding officer should modify milestones based on complexity, issues, and desire for fair and expeditious resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Milestones for hearings under Subpart L (COLs, renewals, amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model schedule milestones for proceedings under 10 CFR Part 2, Subpart L, keyed to NRC staff review schedule for safety/environmental evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key milestones (examples): within 140 days of publication of notice: presiding officer decision on intervention petitions and admission of contentions; within 55 days of decision granting intervention: presiding officer to set initial schedule based on staff SER schedule; within 30 days of issuance of SER/NEPA: proposed new/amended contentions or motions for summary disposition due; within 85 days of SER/NEPA: presiding officer decision on admission of new/amended contentions and motions; within 14 days after decision: parties update mandatory disclosures; within 115 days of SER/NEPA: motions for summary disposition due; within 155 days: written direct testimony filed; within 175 days: evidentiary hearing begins; within 90 days of end of hearing/closing record: presiding officer issues initial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Milestones for hearings on license transfer under Subpart M
rubrics_metrics.description: Model milestones for proceedings under 10 CFR Part 2, Subpart M (license transfer applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key milestones (examples): within 100 days of FR notice: presiding officer decision on intervention petitions and admission of contentions; within 30 days of order granting hearing petitions: NRC staff and parties complete mandatory disclosures; within 12 days of completion of mandatory disclosures: presiding officer issues scheduling order; within 45 days of scheduling order: oral hearing commences; within 25 days after hearing ends: presiding officer certifies hearing record to the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Milestones for hearings under Subpart N (expedited proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model milestones for enforcement proceedings conducted under 10 CFR Part 2, Subpart N (expedited procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key milestones (examples): within 20 days of enforcement order: person files answer and requests for hearing including joint motion to use Subpart N; within 50 days: presiding officer decision on hearing requests and confirmation of use of Subpart N; within 30 days of presiding officer decision granting hearing: mandatory disclosures complete; within 40 days: prehearing conference to specify issues and set schedules; within 60 days: evidentiary hearing begins; within 30 days of end of hearing and closing of record: presiding officer issues initial decision. Only mandatory disclosures (per § 2.336) are provided as discovery under Subpart N.
